record.paper_title: Recent advances in open billiards with some open problems
record.original_question: For an open quantum billiard, modeled by the Helmholtz equation (∇^2 + k^2)ψ = 0 with Dirichlet boundary conditions and resonance solutions whose wavenumber k has negative imaginary part, is the number of resonant states with Re(k_n) < k and Im(k_n) > -C for a positive constant C of order k^(d_H+1) as k tends to infinity, where d_H is the partial Hausdorff dimension of the classical non-escaping set?

evidence.quote: If the billiard is open, for example consisting of a finite region containing obstacles that do not prevent the particle escaping to infinity, the Helmholtz equation has resonance solutions where k has negative imaginary part.

Open problem 15. The fractal Weyl conjecture: The number of states with Re(kn) < k and Im(kn) > −C for some positive constant C is of order k dH+1 where again k → ∞ and dH is the partial Hausdorff dimension of the non-escaping set.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider an open quantum billiard in $\mathbb{R}^d$ ($d\ge 2$) consisting of a region containing a finite collection of compact obstacles such that classical trajectories may escape to infinity. The stationary wavefunctions $\psi$ satisfy the Helmholtz equation
$$(\nabla^2 + k^2)\psi = 0$$
with Dirichlet boundary conditions on the obstacles and outgoing radiation conditions at infinity. Resonances are non-trivial solutions of this boundary-value problem corresponding to complex wavenumbers $k_n$ with $\operatorname{Im}(k_n) < 0$.

Let $K$ denote the classical non-escaping (trapped) set, i.e., the set of phase-space points whose forward and backward trajectories under the billiard flow remain in a bounded region forever, and let $d_H$ be the partial Hausdorff dimension of $K$ (the Hausdorff dimension of its intersection with a Poincaré section, or equivalently $\dim_H K = 2 d_H + 1$).

For a fixed constant $C > 0$, let
$$N(k, C) \;=\; \#\{ n : \operatorname{Re}(k_n) < k,\ \operatorname{Im}(k_n) > -C \}.$$

Prove or disprove: as $k \to \infty$,
$$N(k, C) \;=\; \Theta\!\left(k^{\,d_H + 1}\right).$$
That is, establish the fractal Weyl law for the number of scattering resonances of the open billiard with real part bounded by $k$ and imaginary part bounded below by $-C$, with the exponent given by $d_H + 1$, where $d_H$ is the partial Hausdorff dimension of the classical non-escaping set.
artifact.category_tag: fractal Weyl law for open quantum billiards
artifact.status_search_result: The fractal Weyl conjecture remains open in general. Sharp upper bounds of the conjectured order have been established (Sjöstrand, Zworski, Nonnenmacher–Sjöstrand–Zworski, Dyatlov, Naud) and there is strong numerical evidence (e.g., three-disk scatterers), but a matching lower bound—the full asymptotic—has not been proved. A 2025 preprint even reports counter-examples to the fractal Weyl law for certain semiclassical resonances, indicating that the conjecture as stated does not hold universally and is still actively investigated.

status_evidence.title: Fractal Weyl law for open quantum chaotic maps
status_evidence.snippet: Establishes fractal upper bounds on resonance counts; the lower bound (full law) remains conjectural.
status_evidence.claim: Only the upper bound of the fractal Weyl law is known in general.

status_evidence.title: Resonance states of the three-disk scattering system
status_evidence.snippet: Numerical computations validate the fractal Weyl law over a large semiclassical range.
status_evidence.claim: Strong numerical evidence supports the conjecture but no full proof.

status_evidence.title: Counter-examples to the fractal Weyl law for semiclassical resonances
status_evidence.snippet: Presents counter-examples to the fractal Weyl law for semiclassical resonances.
status_evidence.claim: Conjecture is not universally valid; status remains unsettled.

status_evidence.title: Improved fractal Weyl bounds for convex cocompact hyperbolic surfaces
status_evidence.snippet: Improves upper bounds on resonance counting functions.
status_evidence.claim: Active research continues to refine bounds rather than settle the conjecture.
